records.title: Sumerian scribes count in sixties
records.note: Accounting tablets from Uruk count in units of 60; the later Babylonian place-value form survives in our 60-minute hours and 360-degree circles.

records.title: Step Pyramid of Djoser, the first monumental stone building
records.note: Credited to the official Imhotep, six stacked stone terraces mark the start of large-scale cut-stone architecture.

records.title: Great Pyramid of Giza
records.note: Squared to the cardinal points with remarkable accuracy, it stayed the tallest human-made structure for close to four thousand years.

records.title: Plimpton 322 tabulates Pythagorean triples
records.note: An Old Babylonian clay tablet lists whole-number sides of right triangles more than a thousand years before Pythagoras.

records.title: Babylonians record the cycle of Venus
records.note: Twenty-one years of Venus appearing and vanishing, observed under King Ammisaduqa, among the oldest astronomical records kept.

records.title: Edwin Smith Papyrus, the oldest surgical treatise
records.note: Forty-eight injury cases, each with examination, diagnosis and treatment, including the earliest known written account of the brain.

records.title: Ebers Papyrus records hundreds of remedies
records.note: A long Egyptian medical scroll on the heart, eyes, skin and digestion, with some 700 prescriptions and spells.

records.title: Rhind Mathematical Papyrus
records.note: The scribe Ahmes copies 84 problems on fractions, areas, volumes and equations, with a value for π close to 3.16.

records.title: Water clock at Karnak
records.note: The oldest surviving water clock, an alabaster vessel from the reign of Amenhotep III, tells the night hours by its outflow.

records.title: Shang oracle bones record eclipses
records.note: Divination bones from the Shang capital note eclipses of the Moon, the earliest Chinese astronomical records.

records.title: Babylonian Astronomical Diaries begin
records.note: Night-by-night records of the Moon, planets, weather and prices, kept for some six centuries: antiquity’s longest scientific record.

records.title: Sushruta Samhita: surgery in ancient India
records.note: A Sanskrit treatise describing hundreds of operations and instruments, including rebuilding the nose with a flap of skin.

records.title: Thales predicts a solar eclipse
records.note: Herodotus reports that Thales foretold the eclipse that stopped a battle between the Lydians and the Medes.

records.title: Tunnel of Eupalinos dug from both ends
records.note: A kilometre-long aqueduct tunnel cut from two sides that met near the middle, an early triumph of applied geometry.

records.title: Pythagoreans: number underlies nature
records.note: The community Pythagoras led at Croton treats number as the key to the world; the right-triangle theorem carries his name.

records.title: Alcmaeon places the mind in the brain
records.note: From dissection he traces the optic nerves and argues that the brain, not the heart, is the seat of perception and thought.

records.title: Leucippus and Democritus propose atoms
records.note: Everything is made of tiny indivisible particles moving in empty space, a guess chemistry would vindicate two millennia later.

records.title: Hippocratic medicine: disease has natural causes
records.note: The Hippocratic writings explain illness without the gods and stress observation, prognosis and a physician’s duties.

records.title: Eudoxus: proportion, exhaustion and nested spheres
records.note: A theory of ratios that copes with irrational lengths, the method of exhaustion, and the first geometric model of the planets.

records.title: Aristotle’s History of Animals founds zoology
records.note: Hundreds of species, many studied on Lesbos, described and grouped by anatomy, reproduction and way of life.

records.title: Euclid’s Elements
records.note: Thirteen books that derive geometry and number theory from definitions and axioms, the model of proof for two thousand years.

records.title: Theophrastus classifies plants
records.note: Some 500 plants described by form, habitat and use, earning Aristotle’s successor the title of father of botany.

records.title: Herophilus dissects the human body
records.note: Systematic human dissection separates nerves from tendons, describes the brain’s ventricles and ties the pulse to the heart.

records.title: Aristarchus puts the Sun at the centre
records.note: Reckoning that the Sun is far larger than the Earth, he proposes that the Earth goes round it, 1,800 years before Copernicus.

records.title: Archimedes: buoyancy and the lever
records.note: A floating body displaces its own weight of fluid; with the law of the lever, the first results of statics and hydrostatics.

records.title: Archimedes pins π between 3 10⁄71 and 3 1⁄7
records.note: Polygons of 96 sides drawn inside and outside a circle squeeze π between two fractions, an early limit argument.

records.title: Ctesibius: the force pump and a self-regulating clock
records.note: Machines driven by air and water pressure, including a float-regulated water clock that set the pattern for centuries.

records.title: Eratosthenes measures the Earth
records.note: Noon shadows at Syene and Alexandria give a circumference close to the true 40,000 km.

records.title: Apollonius names the conic sections
records.note: Ellipse, parabola and hyperbola studied as slices of a cone: the curves Kepler and Newton would need.

records.title: Hipparchus finds precession and begins trigonometry
records.note: Comparing his star positions with older ones reveals the slow drift of the equinoxes; his table of chords starts trigonometry.

records.title: Antikythera mechanism
records.note: Recovered from a shipwreck, this geared bronze calculator modelled the Sun and Moon, predicted eclipses and tracked the games.

records.title: The Yellow Emperor’s Inner Classic
records.note: The founding text of Chinese medicine: organs, channels, pulse diagnosis and the balance of yin and yang.

records.title: Maya Long Count calendar
records.note: Stela 2 at Chiapa de Corzo carries the oldest known Long Count date; Maya place-value numbers came to include a zero.

records.title: Vitruvius writes On Architecture
records.note: Ten books on building, water supply, machines and sundials, the only major work on architecture surviving from antiquity.

records.title: Hero of Alexandria spins a sphere with steam
records.note: The aeolipile, turned by jets of steam, appears among Hero’s pneumatic devices, automata and surveying instruments.

records.title: Pliny’s Natural History
records.note: A 37-book encyclopedia of astronomy, geography, animals, plants, medicine and minerals, read throughout the Middle Ages.

records.title: Cai Lun improves papermaking
records.note: A court official presents paper made from bark, hemp, rags and old fishing nets: cheap writing material that spread across Asia.

records.title: The Pantheon’s concrete dome
records.note: Roman concrete with volcanic ash spans 43 metres, still the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world.

records.title: Zhang Heng’s seismoscope
records.note: A bronze vessel that dropped a ball from a dragon’s mouth to signal a distant earthquake and the direction it came from.

records.title: Ptolemy’s Almagest
records.note: An Earth-centred model of epicycles and equants that predicted planetary positions well enough to be used for 1,400 years.

records.title: Ptolemy maps the world by coordinates
records.note: Thousands of places listed by latitude and longitude, with instructions for projecting the globe onto a flat map.

records.title: Galen’s experimental physiology
records.note: Experiments on animals show that arteries carry blood and that cutting nerves from the spine paralyses muscles.

records.title: Diophantus writes the Arithmetica
records.note: Problems solved with abbreviations for unknowns and powers, an early step towards algebraic notation.

records.title: Liu Hui’s commentary on the Nine Chapters
records.note: Proofs for the classic Chinese problem book, with negative numbers, elimination for linear systems and π ≈ 3.1416.

records.title: Hypatia teaches mathematics and astronomy
records.note: Head of a philosophical school, she wrote commentaries on Diophantus and Apollonius and helped edit Ptolemy’s Almagest.

records.title: Zu Chongzhi computes π to seven digits
records.note: π lies between 3.1415926 and 3.1415927, with the fraction 355/113: a record that stood for almost a thousand years.

records.title: Aryabhata’s Aryabhatiya
records.note: Place-value arithmetic, a sine table, π ≈ 3.1416 and the proposal that the Earth turns on its axis.

records.title: Philoponus challenges Aristotle’s physics
records.note: Heavy and light bodies fall at nearly the same speed, and a thrown object keeps an impressed force, an early idea of impetus.

records.title: Hagia Sophia’s dome on pendentives
records.note: Two mathematicians design a vast dome carried on curved triangles over a square plan, a new solution in engineering.

records.title: Brahmagupta gives rules for zero and negatives
records.note: The first text to treat zero as a number, with rules for adding, subtracting and multiplying debts, fortunes and zero.

records.title: Sun Simiao’s prescriptions worth a thousand gold
records.note: A thirty-volume medical encyclopedia covering women’s and children’s health and diet, opening with a code of medical ethics.

records.title: Dunhuang Star Chart
records.note: The oldest complete star atlas known, drawing well over a thousand stars of the Chinese sky.

records.title: Yi Xing’s water-driven celestial globe
records.note: A water-powered globe with an escapement-like mechanism to mark the hours; Yi Xing also led a nationwide survey of the meridian.

records.title: Laboratory alchemy of the Jabirian corpus
records.note: Writings attributed to Jabir describe distillation, crystallisation and the preparation of acids, and sort substances by their properties.

records.title: Al-Khwarizmi’s algebra
records.note: Systematic solution of linear and quadratic equations; “algebra” comes from the book’s title and “algorithm” from his name.

records.title: Al-Kindi invents frequency analysis
records.note: Substitution ciphers are broken by counting how often each letter occurs: the start of cryptanalysis.

records.title: The Banu Musa’s Book of Ingenious Devices
records.note: About a hundred mechanisms, from automatic valves and self-trimming lamps to a programmable mechanical flute player.

records.title: Chinese alchemists discover gunpowder
records.note: A Taoist text warns that heating saltpetre, sulphur and charcoal together makes flames burst out: the first record of gunpowder.

records.title: Al-Battani measures the solar year
records.note: Decades of observations at Raqqa give the length of the year to within about two minutes and improve on Ptolemy’s values.

records.title: Al-Razi tells smallpox from measles
records.note: His treatise on smallpox and measles gives the first clear clinical description separating the two diseases.

records.title: Al-Sufi’s Book of Fixed Stars
records.note: An illustrated star catalogue with the first written description of the Andromeda Galaxy, a “small cloud”.

records.title: Ibn Sahl states the law of refraction
records.note: A treatise on burning mirrors and lenses gives the sine law of refraction six centuries before Snell.

records.title: Al-Zahrawi’s illustrated surgery
records.note: The last volume of his medical encyclopedia draws some 200 surgical instruments and was used in European schools for centuries.

records.title: Ibn al-Haytham’s Book of Optics
records.note: Experiments with light, mirrors and the camera obscura show that we see by light entering the eye: a model of experimental method.

records.title: Al-Biruni measures the Earth from a hilltop
records.note: The dip of the horizon seen from a hill near Nandana gives the Earth’s radius to within a few per cent.

records.title: Avicenna’s Canon of Medicine
records.note: A five-book synthesis of Greek and Islamic medicine with rules for testing drugs, taught in Europe until the 1600s.

records.title: Bi Sheng invents movable type
records.note: Characters of baked clay set in an iron frame, described by Shen Kuo, four centuries before Gutenberg.

records.title: Song astronomers record the Crab supernova
records.note: A “guest star” bright enough to see by day for 23 days; its remnant is the Crab Nebula.

records.title: Omar Khayyam: cubic equations and a new calendar
records.note: He classifies and solves cubic equations with conic sections, and leads the reform of the Jalali solar calendar at Isfahan.

records.title: Shen Kuo describes the magnetic compass
records.note: The Dream Pool Essays describe a magnetised-needle compass and magnetic declination, and argue that landscapes change over time.

records.title: Su Song’s astronomical clock tower
records.note: A twelve-metre water-driven tower with an escapement that turned an armillary sphere and a celestial globe and struck the hours.

records.title: Bhaskara II’s Crown of Treatises
records.note: The head of the Ujjain observatory solves Pell’s equation by the cyclic method and touches on ideas of the derivative.

records.title: Hildegard of Bingen’s natural history
records.note: Books on plants, animals, stones and remedies, the first natural history and medicine written by a woman in Germany.

records.title: Al-Idrisi’s world map for Roger II
records.note: Fifteen years of travellers’ reports compiled at Palermo make the most accurate world map of the Middle Ages.
people: Abu Abdullah Muhammad al-Idrisi al-Qurtubi al-Hasani as-Sabti

records.title: Fibonacci’s Liber Abaci
records.note: Hindu–Arabic numerals and place-value arithmetic for European merchants, with the rabbit problem behind the Fibonacci numbers.

records.title: Al-Jazari’s Book of Ingenious Mechanical Devices
records.note: Fifty machines, from crank-driven pumps to programmable automata, each drawn with instructions for building it.

records.title: Ibn al-Nafis describes the pulmonary circulation
records.note: Blood passes from the right side of the heart to the left through the lungs, not through pores in the wall as Galen taught.

records.title: The Maragheh observatory and the Tusi couple
records.note: Al-Tusi’s observatory produces new tables, and his two rolling circles turn circular motion into straight-line motion.

records.title: Roger Bacon’s Opus Majus urges experiment
records.note: A treatise for the Pope on optics, mathematics and “experimental science”, describing lenses that magnify.

records.title: Peter Peregrinus defines magnetic poles
records.note: Written during the siege of Lucera, the letter describes north and south poles, attraction and repulsion, and a pivoted compass.

records.title: Guo Shoujing’s Season-Granting calendar
records.note: New instruments and a network of observatories fix the year at 365.2425 days, the value of the later Gregorian calendar.

records.title: Eyeglasses invented in Italy
records.note: A Pisan sermon of 1306 says spectacles had been invented about twenty years before: convex lenses for reading.

records.title: Mondino de Luzzi’s manual of dissection
records.note: Written from public dissections at Bologna, his Anathomia was the standard anatomy text for two centuries.

records.title: Richard of Wallingford’s astronomical clock
records.note: Designed for St Albans Abbey, a mechanical clock showing the Sun, Moon, tides and eclipses, among the most complex of its age.

records.title: Oxford Calculators prove the mean speed theorem
records.note: A uniformly accelerating body covers the same distance as one moving at its mean speed, a result Galileo later used.

records.title: Ibn al-Shatir’s planetary models
records.note: Models of the Moon and planets without Ptolemy’s equant, matching ones Copernicus used two centuries later.

records.title: Oresme draws graphs of changing quantities
records.note: Plotting intensity against time anticipates coordinate graphs and gives a geometric proof of the mean speed theorem.

records.title: Jikji printed with movable metal type
records.note: A Buddhist text printed at Heungdeok Temple, the oldest surviving book made with movable metal type.

records.title: Madhava’s infinite series
records.note: The Kerala school expands π, sine and cosine as infinite series, some 250 years before Newton and Leibniz.

records.title: Al-Kashi computes π to 16 decimal places
records.note: A polygon with 805 million sides gives a record accuracy that stood for 180 years.

records.title: Jang Yeong-sil’s self-striking water clock
records.note: An automatic water clock for the Joseon court that announced the hours with bells, gongs and drums.

records.title: Ulugh Beg’s star catalogue
records.note: From a giant meridian arc at Samarkand, positions of nearly a thousand stars: the best catalogue between Ptolemy and Tycho.

records.title: Gutenberg’s printing press
records.note: Cast metal type, oil-based ink and a screw press make books cheap enough to spread learning across Europe.

records.title: Standard rain gauges across Joseon Korea
records.note: Identical gauges sent to every district produce the first systematic national records of rainfall.

records.title: Nilakantha Somayaji revises the planets’ orbits
records.note: A Kerala astronomer makes Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn circle the Sun, which in turn circles the Earth.

records.title: Waldseemüller’s map names America
records.note: A world map showing a separate continent across the Atlantic, labelled “America” after Amerigo Vespucci.

records.title: Leonardo’s anatomical studies
records.note: Drawings made from dissection, of the heart’s valves, the spine and the foetus in the womb, far ahead of their time.

records.title: Paracelsus brings chemistry into medicine
records.note: Lecturing at Basel he rejects the four humours for mineral remedies and careful dosing: the dose decides what is a poison.

records.title: Copernicus: the Earth orbits the Sun
records.note: A Sun-centred system explains the planets’ backward loops as an effect of the Earth’s own motion.

records.title: Vesalius’s Fabric of the Human Body
records.note: Seven illustrated books of anatomy from dissection, correcting hundreds of Galen’s errors.

records.title: Cardano solves cubic and quartic equations
records.note: General solutions of third- and fourth-degree equations, forcing mathematicians to handle square roots of negative numbers.

records.title: Fracastoro’s theory of contagion
records.note: Diseases spread by tiny seeds, passed by touch, on objects or through the air: an early germ theory.

records.title: Gessner’s History of Animals
records.note: A vast illustrated encyclopedia of animals that marks the beginning of modern zoology.

records.title: Agricola’s On the Nature of Metals
records.note: The first systematic treatise on mining and metallurgy, with woodcuts of pumps, ventilation and smelting.

records.title: Mercator’s projection
records.note: A world map on which a line of constant compass bearing is straight, the standard chart for navigation ever since.

records.title: Tycho’s new star
records.note: A supernova shows no parallax, so it lies among the fixed stars: the heavens are not unchanging.

records.title: Tycho builds Uraniborg
records.note: An island observatory whose instruments measure star positions to about an arcminute, the data Kepler later used.

records.title: Li Shizhen’s Compendium of Materia Medica
records.note: Twenty-seven years of work describe nearly 1,900 drugs from plants, animals and minerals, with over a thousand illustrations.

records.title: Stevin’s decimal fractions
records.note: A short pamphlet makes decimal fractions practical for trade and measurement and calls for decimal units.

records.title: The compound microscope
records.note: Spectacle makers in Middelburg put two lenses in a tube; who did it first is still disputed.

records.title: Gilbert: the Earth is a great magnet
records.note: Experiments with a magnetised sphere explain the compass needle and introduce the word “electric”.

records.title: Galileo’s law of falling bodies
records.note: Balls rolled down inclined planes show that the distance fallen grows with the square of the time.

records.title: The telescope is patented
records.note: Lipperhey asks the Dutch States-General for a patent on a tube for seeing distant things as if they were near.

records.title: Kepler: planets move in ellipses
records.note: From Tycho’s observations of Mars, the first two laws: elliptical orbits, and equal areas swept in equal times.

records.title: Galileo’s telescope finds Jupiter’s moons
records.note: Mountains on the Moon, countless stars in the Milky Way and four moons circling Jupiter.

records.title: Napier’s logarithms
records.note: Tables that turn multiplication into addition, cutting the labour of astronomical calculation.

records.title: Kepler’s third law
records.note: The square of a planet’s orbital period is proportional to the cube of its distance from the Sun.

records.title: Harvey: the blood circulates
records.note: Measurement shows the heart pumps far more blood than the body could make, so it must flow round a circuit.

records.title: Descartes and Fermat unite algebra and geometry
records.note: Curves become equations in coordinates: analytic geometry, reached independently by Fermat.

records.title: Song Yingxing’s Works of Nature and Human Craft
records.note: An illustrated encyclopedia of Ming technology: farming, silk, salt, ceramics, metals, paper and weapons.

records.title: Galileo’s Two New Sciences
records.note: Written under house arrest at Arcetri: projectiles follow parabolas, and a mathematical science of the strength of materials.

records.title: Pascal’s calculating machine
records.note: A geared adding machine built to help his father with tax accounts, among the first mechanical calculators.

records.title: Torricelli’s barometer
records.note: A tube of mercury upended in a bowl leaves a vacuum at the top, held up by the weight of the air.

records.title: Von Guericke’s air pump and evacuated hemispheres
records.note: Teams of horses cannot pull apart two copper hemispheres emptied of air, a public demonstration of air pressure.

records.title: Pascal and Fermat found probability theory
records.note: Letters on dividing the stakes of an unfinished game set out the mathematics of expected value.

records.title: Huygens finds Titan and Saturn’s ring
records.note: A better telescope reveals Saturn’s largest moon and explains the planet’s odd shape as a thin flat ring.

records.title: Huygens’s pendulum clock
records.note: Clocks become accurate to seconds rather than minutes a day, making precise physics and astronomy possible.

records.title: Malpighi sees the capillaries
records.note: Under the microscope a frog’s lung shows the tiny vessels linking arteries to veins, completing Harvey’s circuit.

records.title: Boyle’s law
records.note: Experiments with Hooke’s air pump show that a gas’s pressure varies inversely with its volume.

records.title: Hooke’s Micrographia names the cell
records.note: Engravings of a flea, a fly’s eye and cork, whose tiny compartments Hooke calls “cells”.

records.title: Newton develops calculus
records.note: At home during the plague years Newton works out his method of fluxions, published only decades later.

records.title: Newton’s reflecting telescope
records.note: A curved mirror in place of lenses removes the colour fringes that troubled refracting telescopes.

records.title: Brand isolates phosphorus
records.note: Boiling down urine in search of the philosopher’s stone yields a glowing substance, the first element found by a known person.

records.title: Steno’s principles of rock layers
records.note: Layers of rock are laid down in order, the oldest at the bottom, and fossils are the remains of living things.

records.title: Cassini and Richer measure the Solar System
records.note: Simultaneous sightings of Mars from Paris and Cayenne give the first good estimate of the distance to the Sun.

records.title: Newton: white light is a mixture of colours
records.note: Prism experiments show sunlight splitting into a spectrum, with each colour bending by its own fixed amount.

records.title: Leeuwenhoek sees microorganisms
records.note: Tiny single-lens microscopes reveal “little animals”, bacteria and protists, in rainwater and on teeth.

records.title: Rømer finds light has a finite speed
records.note: Eclipses of Jupiter’s moon Io come late when Jupiter is far from the Earth: light takes time to travel.

records.title: Huygens’s wave theory of light
records.note: Every point on a wavefront sends out new wavelets, explaining reflection and refraction.

records.title: Seki Takakazu introduces determinants
records.note: A Japanese mathematician uses determinants to eliminate unknowns from equations, ten years before Leibniz.

records.title: Leibniz publishes the calculus
records.note: A paper in Acta Eruditorum introduces the d and ∫ notation still used today.

records.title: Newton’s Principia: motion and universal gravitation
records.note: Three laws of motion and an inverse-square law of gravity explain falling bodies, orbits, tides and Kepler’s laws.

records.title: Savery’s steam pump
records.note: Patented to drain mines, the first commercial use of steam to do work.

records.title: Halley predicts his comet’s return
records.note: The comets of 1531, 1607 and 1682 are one body on a 76-year orbit; its return in 1758 confirms Newton’s gravity.

records.title: Merian paints the insects of Suriname
records.note: From two years’ fieldwork in Suriname, insects shown with their food plants through every stage of life.

records.title: Darby smelts iron with coke
records.note: Coke instead of charcoal frees iron-making from scarce wood, a foundation of the Industrial Revolution.

records.title: Newcomen’s atmospheric engine
records.note: The first practical steam engine, pumping water from a coal mine near Dudley Castle.

records.title: Fahrenheit’s mercury thermometer
records.note: Reliable mercury thermometers and, ten years later, the temperature scale that carries his name.

records.title: Onesimus’s inoculation saves lives in Boston
records.note: West African knowledge shared by Onesimus leads Boylston to inoculate during an epidemic, with far fewer deaths among those treated.

records.title: Montagu brings smallpox inoculation to Britain
records.note: Having seen the Ottoman practice in Constantinople, she has her daughter inoculated during a London epidemic.

records.title: Bradley discovers the aberration of starlight
records.note: Stars shift through the year because of the Earth’s motion: direct proof that the Earth orbits the Sun.

records.title: Gray shows electricity can be conducted
records.note: Charge travels hundreds of feet along a thread hung on silk, separating conductors from insulators.

records.title: Hadley explains the trade winds
records.note: The Earth’s rotation turns air flowing towards the equator into steady easterly winds.

records.title: Linnaeus’s System of Nature
records.note: A nested classification of nature into kingdoms, classes, orders, genera and species.

records.title: Euler and the bridges of Königsberg
records.note: Proving that no walk crosses each bridge exactly once, Euler founds graph theory.

records.title: The Earth is flattened at the poles
records.note: Measuring a degree of latitude in Lapland confirms Newton’s prediction of an Earth squashed at the poles.

records.title: Bernoulli’s Hydrodynamica
records.note: Faster-flowing fluid exerts less pressure; the book also explains gas pressure as molecules striking the walls.

records.title: Émilie du Châtelet’s Foundations of Physics
records.note: She argues that a body’s energy goes as the square of its speed and later translates Newton’s Principia with a commentary.

records.title: The Celsius temperature scale
records.note: A hundred degrees between the freezing and boiling points of water, originally numbered the other way round.

records.title: The Leyden jar stores electric charge
records.note: A water-filled jar lined with metal holds a powerful charge: the first capacitor.

records.title: Lind’s controlled trial for scurvy
records.note: Twelve sick sailors get six different treatments; the two given oranges and lemons recover, an early controlled clinical trial.

records.title: Euler’s Introduction to the Analysis of the Infinite
records.note: Functions become the central objects of analysis, and exponentials are tied to sines and cosines.

records.title: Buffon’s Natural History
records.note: A vast survey of nature that hints at species changing and at an Earth far older than scripture implied.

records.title: Franklin: lightning is electricity
records.note: Experiments Franklin proposed, tried in France and with his kite, show lightning is an electrical discharge.

records.title: Linnaeus gives every plant a two-part name
records.note: Genus plus species for every known plant: the binomial names biology still uses.

records.title: Black identifies carbon dioxide
records.note: “Fixed air” released from magnesia alba is a distinct gas, shown by careful weighing: quantitative chemistry begins.

records.title: Harrison’s marine chronometer
records.note: His H4 watch keeps time across an Atlantic voyage to within seconds, solving the problem of longitude at sea.

records.title: Morgagni founds pathological anatomy
records.note: Some 700 autopsies tie symptoms in life to damage in particular organs.

records.title: Lomonosov detects an atmosphere on Venus
records.note: As Venus crosses the Sun a bright rim appears around it: the planet has an atmosphere.

records.title: Bayes’s theorem
records.note: Published after his death by Price: how to update the probability of a hypothesis as evidence comes in.

records.title: Cavendish isolates hydrogen
records.note: “Inflammable air” from metals and acid is a distinct, very light gas; later he shows it burns to make water.

records.title: Watt’s separate condenser
records.note: Condensing steam outside the cylinder cuts fuel use by about three-quarters, making steam power economical everywhere.

records.title: Daniel Rutherford isolates nitrogen
records.note: Air in which a candle has burned, stripped of fixed air, still will not support life or flame.

records.title: Oxygen discovered
records.note: Priestley gets “dephlogisticated air” by heating mercury oxide; Scheele had already found it on his own.

records.title: Schiehallion experiment weighs the Earth
records.note: The pull of a Scottish mountain on a plumb line gives the first estimate of the Earth’s mean density.

records.title: Lavoisier explains combustion
records.note: Burning is combination with oxygen, not the release of an imagined substance called phlogiston.

records.title: Ingenhousz: plants need light to refresh air
records.note: Only the green parts of plants, and only in sunlight, give off the air that keeps animals alive.

records.title: William Herschel discovers Uranus
records.note: The first planet found with a telescope doubles the known size of the Solar System.

records.title: Michell imagines “dark stars”
records.note: A star massive enough would hold back its own light: the first idea of a black hole.

records.title: Montgolfier balloon carries people aloft
records.note: The first crewed free flight drifts across Paris for about 25 minutes.

records.title: Coulomb’s law
records.note: A torsion balance shows that electric force falls off with the square of the distance.

records.title: Hutton’s Theory of the Earth
records.note: Slow erosion, deposition and uplift, repeated without end, imply an Earth vastly older than anyone thought.

records.title: Withering’s foxglove for heart failure
records.note: A folk remedy tested on 163 patients becomes a standard treatment for dropsy.

records.title: Caroline Herschel discovers a comet
records.note: The first of eight comets she found; she becomes the first woman in Britain paid for scientific work.

records.title: Lavoisier’s Elementary Treatise of Chemistry
records.note: A list of elements, a new system of names and conservation of mass; Marie-Anne Lavoisier drew its plates.

records.title: Klaproth discovers uranium
records.note: Found in pitchblende and named after the recently discovered planet.

records.title: Galvani’s animal electricity
records.note: Frog legs twitch when touched with two different metals, linking nerves and electricity.

records.title: Chladni: meteorites fall from space
records.note: Stones and masses of iron fall from the sky, he argues, a view confirmed by the shower at L’Aigle in 1803.

records.title: Cuvier proves that species go extinct
records.note: Mammoth and mastodon bones differ from living elephants, so whole kinds of animal have died out.

records.title: Laplace’s nebular hypothesis
records.note: The Solar System condensed from a rotating cloud of gas, refining an idea Kant had put forward in 1755.

records.title: Jenner’s smallpox vaccine
records.note: Cowpox taken from a milkmaid protects a boy from smallpox: the first vaccine.

records.title: Cavendish weighs the Earth
records.note: A torsion balance measures the tiny pull between lead spheres, giving the Earth’s density and, later, G.

records.title: The metre is defined from the Earth
records.note: A survey of the meridian from Dunkirk to Barcelona fixes the metre, made in platinum in 1799.

records.title: Herschel discovers infrared
records.note: A thermometer beyond the red end of a prism’s spectrum warms most of all: invisible light.

records.title: Volta’s battery
records.note: A stack of zinc and copper discs separated by brine gives the first steady electric current.

records.title: Ceres, the first asteroid
records.note: Piazzi spots Ceres on New Year’s night; Gauss’s new orbit method lets astronomers find it again.

records.title: Gauss’s Disquisitiones Arithmeticae
records.note: Modular arithmetic and quadratic reciprocity turn number theory into a systematic science.

records.title: Young shows light interferes
records.note: Overlapping beams of light make bright and dark bands, strong evidence that light is a wave.

records.title: Ritter discovers ultraviolet
records.note: Silver chloride darkens fastest just beyond the violet end of the spectrum.

records.title: Dalton’s atomic theory
records.note: Each element is made of identical atoms with a characteristic weight, combining in simple ratios.

records.title: Hanaoka Seishū operates under general anaesthesia
records.note: A herbal anaesthetic lets him remove a breast tumour, forty years before ether was used in the West.

records.title: Jacquard’s punched-card loom
records.note: Chains of punched cards set the weaving pattern, an ancestor of programmable machines.

records.title: Trevithick’s steam locomotive
records.note: The first railway journey under steam hauls ten tons of iron and seventy men along a tramway.

records.title: Davy isolates potassium and sodium
records.note: A large battery splits molten potash and soda, revealing violently reactive new metals.

records.title: Humboldt’s geography of plants
records.note: A cross-section of Chimborazo shows vegetation zones changing with altitude as with latitude: the start of biogeography.

records.title: Lamarck’s theory of evolution
records.note: Species change over time: the first full theory of evolution, though driven by inherited acquired traits.

records.title: Avogadro’s hypothesis
records.note: Equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure hold equal numbers of molecules.

records.title: Fraunhofer maps dark lines in sunlight
records.note: A precision spectroscope shows hundreds of dark lines in the Sun’s spectrum, later the key to what stars are made of.

records.title: William Smith’s geological map of Britain
records.note: The first geological map of a whole country, matching rock layers by the fossils they contain.

records.title: Sophie Germain’s theory of vibrating plates
records.note: Her prize-winning memoir on vibrating elastic surfaces lays groundwork for the theory of elasticity.

records.title: Laennec’s stethoscope
records.note: A rolled paper tube, then a wooden cylinder, lets doctors hear the heart and lungs clearly.

records.title: Fresnel’s wave theory of diffraction
records.note: His theory predicts a bright spot in the shadow of a disc; Arago looks, and finds it.
institutions: Corps of bridges, waters and forests

records.title: Ørsted links electricity and magnetism
records.note: A wire carrying current deflects a compass needle.

records.title: Cauchy makes calculus rigorous
records.note: Limits and continuity defined precisely, ending a century of loose reasoning about infinitely small quantities.

records.title: Faraday’s electric motor
records.note: A current-carrying wire circles continuously around a magnet: electricity turned into motion.

records.title: Babbage’s Difference Engine
records.note: A design for a machine to compute and print mathematical tables automatically.

records.title: Fourier’s analytic theory of heat
records.note: Any periodic signal can be written as a sum of sines and cosines, a tool now used across science.

records.title: Mary Anning’s plesiosaur
records.note: The first complete skeleton of a long-necked sea reptile, one of the finds that revealed a lost world.

records.title: Carnot’s theory of heat engines
records.note: An engine’s best efficiency depends only on the temperatures it works between: the root of the second law.

records.title: Fourier describes the greenhouse effect
records.note: The atmosphere lets sunlight in but slows the escape of heat, keeping the Earth warmer than it would otherwise be.

records.title: Niépce takes the first photograph
records.note: Bitumen hardened by light over a long exposure records the view from his window.

records.title: Brown sees particles jitter in water
records.note: Tiny particles from pollen dance endlessly, a motion Einstein would explain by molecules colliding.

records.title: Ohm’s law
records.note: The current through a conductor is proportional to the voltage across it.

records.title: Wöhler makes urea from inorganic matter
records.note: A substance known only from living things is made in the laboratory, undermining the idea of a vital force.

records.title: Non-Euclidean geometry
records.note: A consistent geometry in which Euclid’s parallel postulate fails, found by Lobachevsky and, in 1832, by Bolyai.

records.title: Lyell’s Principles of Geology
records.note: The Earth’s features are explained by processes still at work today, acting over immense spans of time.

records.title: Robert Brown names the cell nucleus
records.note: An opaque spot in orchid cells, which he then finds in plant cell after plant cell.

records.title: Faraday discovers electromagnetic induction
records.note: A changing magnetic field drives a current: the principle of every generator and transformer.

records.title: Galois theory
records.note: Set down the night before his fatal duel, his ideas on symmetry decide which equations can be solved by radicals.

records.title: Mary Somerville connects the physical sciences
records.note: A best-selling synthesis of the sciences; a review of it gives English the word “scientist”.

records.title: The Coriolis effect
records.note: Motion in a rotating frame is deflected sideways, which shapes winds and ocean currents.
records.place: École Nationale des Ponts et Chaussées
institutions: École Nationale des Ponts et Chaussées

records.title: The electric telegraph
records.note: Cooke and Wheatstone patent a needle telegraph; Morse’s code and single-wire system follow.

records.title: Bessel measures the distance to a star
records.note: The parallax of 61 Cygni puts it about ten light-years away, the first measured distance to a star.

records.title: Cell theory
records.note: All plants and animals are built of cells, the basic unit of life.

records.title: The daguerreotype
records.note: Silvered plates developed with mercury vapour make photography practical.

records.title: Liebig’s chemistry of plant nutrition
records.note: Plants draw nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium from the soil, the basis of chemical fertilisers.

records.title: Agassiz proposes an ice age
records.note: Boulders and scratched rocks far from today’s glaciers show that ice once covered much of Europe.

records.title: Owen names the dinosaurs
records.note: Megalosaurus, Iguanodon and Hylaeosaurus are grouped as Dinosauria, “terrible lizards”.
records.place: Royal College of Surgeons of England
institutions: Royal College of Surgeons of England

records.title: The Doppler effect
records.note: A wave’s frequency depends on how its source moves relative to the observer.

records.title: Ada Lovelace’s notes on the Analytical Engine
records.note: An algorithm for Bernoulli numbers, and the insight that such a machine could work on symbols, not just numbers.

records.title: Joule’s mechanical equivalent of heat
records.note: Falling weights stirring water warm it by a fixed amount: heat is a form of energy.

records.title: Hamilton’s quaternions
records.note: He carves i² = j² = k² = ijk = −1 into a Dublin bridge: an algebra of rotations in three dimensions.

records.title: Ether anaesthesia demonstrated
records.note: A public operation under ether in Boston launches surgical anaesthesia worldwide.

records.title: Neptune found by calculation
records.note: Le Verrier predicts a planet from Uranus’s wanderings; Galle finds it within a degree of the spot.

records.title: Conservation of energy
records.note: Energy changes form but its total stays the same, reached independently by Mayer, Joule and Helmholtz.

records.title: Semmelweis: wash hands to save mothers
records.note: Washing in chlorinated lime cuts deaths from childbed fever on his ward from about one in ten to one or two in a hundred.

records.title: Maria Mitchell discovers a comet
records.note: The find wins a gold medal from the King of Denmark; she becomes America’s first professional woman astronomer.

records.title: Kelvin’s absolute temperature scale
records.note: A scale starting from absolute zero, the coldest temperature possible.

records.title: The second law of thermodynamics
records.note: Heat never flows by itself from cold to hot; in 1865 Clausius names entropy.

records.title: Foucault’s pendulum shows the Earth turning
records.note: A 67-metre pendulum in the Panthéon slowly turns its plane of swing as the Earth rotates beneath it.

records.title: Boole’s Laws of Thought
records.note: Logic becomes algebra on true and false, the basis of digital circuits.

records.title: John Snow traces cholera to a water pump
records.note: Mapping deaths around the Broad Street pump shows cholera spreads through water, a founding study of epidemiology.

records.title: Riemann’s geometry of curved space
records.note: A lecture extends geometry to any number of dimensions and any curvature: the mathematics of general relativity.

records.title: The Bessemer process
records.note: Blowing air through molten iron burns out the carbon, making steel cheaply and in bulk.

records.title: Eunice Foote: carbon dioxide traps heat
records.note: Glass cylinders of carbon dioxide warm far more in sunlight than air, and she suggests this could change the climate.

records.title: Perkin makes the first synthetic dye
records.note: An attempt to make quinine from coal tar yields a purple dye and launches the chemical industry.

records.title: Neanderthal fossils found
records.note: Bones from a cave in the Neander valley are the first recognised fossils of an extinct kind of human.

records.title: Virchow’s cellular pathology
records.note: Every cell comes from another cell, and disease is a disturbance of cells.

records.title: Nightingale’s statistics of soldiers’ deaths
records.note: Her polar-area diagrams show most soldiers in the Crimea died of preventable disease, driving sanitary reform.

records.title: Wallace’s letter from Ternate
records.note: Wallace reaches natural selection on his own; his essay and Darwin’s notes are read together in London.

records.title: Carrington sees a solar flare
records.note: A white-light flare is followed by the strongest magnetic storm on record, with auroras worldwide and telegraphs failing.

records.title: Darwin’s On the Origin of Species
records.note: Evolution by natural selection explains the diversity and adaptations of life from common ancestors.

records.title: Kirchhoff and Bunsen invent spectral analysis
records.note: Each element emits and absorbs its own lines of colour, revealing what the Sun is made of.

records.title: Tyndall measures which gases absorb heat
records.note: Water vapour and carbon dioxide absorb infrared strongly, while oxygen and nitrogen hardly do.

records.title: Archaeopteryx, between dinosaurs and birds
records.note: A feathered fossil with teeth and a bony tail, found two years after Darwin predicted transitional forms.

records.title: Broca finds the brain’s speech area
records.note: A patient who could say only one word had damage to the left frontal lobe: functions are localised in the brain.

records.title: FitzRoy issues the first public weather forecasts
records.note: Observations gathered by telegraph give storm warnings and daily forecasts printed in The Times.

records.title: Pasteur disproves spontaneous generation
records.note: Boiled broth in swan-neck flasks stays sterile: microbes come only from microbes, a basis of germ theory.

records.title: Kekulé’s benzene ring
records.note: Six carbon atoms in a ring explain benzene’s formula and the chemistry of aromatic compounds.

records.title: Maxwell’s electromagnetic theory of light
records.note: Electricity, magnetism and light are one phenomenon, waves in a field travelling at the speed of light.

records.title: Mendel’s laws of inheritance
records.note: Crossing thousands of pea plants shows traits passed on in discrete units, in predictable ratios.

records.title: Claude Bernard’s experimental medicine
records.note: The body keeps its internal environment constant, the idea later called homeostasis.

records.title: Lister’s antiseptic surgery
records.note: Carbolic acid on wounds and instruments sharply cuts deaths from infection after surgery.

records.title: Nobel patents dynamite
records.note: Nitroglycerine soaked into diatomaceous earth becomes a safe, powerful explosive for mines and tunnels.

records.title: Helium found in the Sun
records.note: A yellow line seen during an eclipse in India fits no known element; Lockyer names it after the Sun.

records.title: Miescher discovers nucleic acid
records.note: A phosphorus-rich substance from the nuclei of white blood cells, “nuclein”, is the first isolation of DNA.

records.title: Mendeleev’s periodic table
records.note: Elements in order of weight fall into families; gaps predict gallium, scandium and germanium.
records.place: St. Petersburg Practical Institute of Technology
institutions: St. Petersburg Practical Institute of Technology

records.title: Boltzmann’s statistical mechanics
records.note: Entropy is tied to the number of ways molecules can be arranged, explaining why time runs one way.

records.title: Cantor’s sizes of infinity
records.note: The real numbers cannot be listed one by one: some infinities are larger than others.

records.title: The tetrahedral carbon atom
records.note: Four bonds pointing to the corners of a tetrahedron explain mirror-image molecules.

records.title: HMS Challenger sounds the deep ocean
records.note: A four-year voyage founds oceanography, finds thousands of new species and records depths in the Mariana Trench.

records.title: Koch proves a bacterium causes anthrax
records.note: Growing anthrax bacilli outside the body and following their life cycle ties one microbe to one disease.

records.title: Gibbs’s chemical thermodynamics
records.note: Free energy and the phase rule explain when reactions run and how phases coexist.
institutions: Yale School of Engineering and Applied Science

records.title: Bell’s telephone
records.note: Speech sent electrically along a wire.

records.title: Hall discovers the moons of Mars
records.note: Phobos and Deimos are found with the great refractor in Washington.

records.title: Edison’s phonograph
records.note: Sound recorded as grooves on tinfoil and played back.

records.title: The practical light bulb
records.note: Carbon filaments in a good vacuum glow for hundreds of hours, bringing electric light into homes.

records.title: Laveran sees the malaria parasite
records.note: A single-celled parasite in a patient’s blood: the first protozoan shown to cause disease.

records.title: Mechnikov discovers phagocytes
records.note: Mobile cells in starfish larvae swarm round and engulf a thorn: the cellular immune response.

records.title: Koch identifies the tuberculosis bacterium
records.note: New staining methods reveal the cause of the deadliest disease of the age.

records.title: Benz’s motor car
records.note: A car built around a petrol engine; Bertha Benz’s long drive in 1888 proves it practical.

records.title: Pasteur’s rabies vaccine
records.note: A course of weakened virus saves a boy bitten by a rabid dog.

records.title: The Michelson–Morley experiment
records.note: Light’s speed is the same in every direction: no sign of the ether thought to carry it.

records.title: Hertz produces radio waves
records.note: Sparks across a gap send out invisible waves that reflect and refract like light, as Maxwell predicted.

records.title: Tesla’s alternating-current motor
records.note: A rotating magnetic field drives a motor without brushes, making AC power systems practical.

records.title: Cajal: the nervous system is made of separate cells
records.note: Golgi’s silver stain shows nerve cells are discrete units meeting at gaps, not one continuous net.

records.title: Antitoxins for diphtheria and tetanus
records.note: Serum from immunised animals neutralises bacterial toxins: the beginning of serum therapy.

records.title: Poincaré finds chaos in the three-body problem
records.note: Three gravitating bodies can move in ways so tangled that long-term prediction becomes impossible.

records.title: Dubois finds Java Man
records.note: A skullcap and thighbone on Java are the first known fossils of Homo erectus.

records.title: Viruses discovered
records.note: Tobacco mosaic disease passes through filters that stop bacteria; in 1898 Beijerinck calls the agent a virus.

records.title: Argon and the noble gases
records.note: A dense leftover in air is a new inert element; neon, krypton and xenon follow, a whole new column of the table.

records.title: J. C. Bose demonstrates millimetre waves
records.note: Microwave apparatus and semiconductor detectors built in Calcutta send signals through walls to ring a bell.

records.title: Marconi’s wireless telegraphy
records.note: Signals sent over a hill near Bologna; by 1901 they cross the Atlantic.

records.title: Röntgen discovers X-rays
records.note: Rays from a discharge tube pass through flesh but not bone; within months doctors are using them.

records.title: Arrhenius calculates warming from carbon dioxide
records.note: Halving or doubling the carbon dioxide in the air would cool or warm the Earth by several degrees.

records.title: Becquerel discovers radioactivity
records.note: Uranium salts fog a wrapped photographic plate in the dark: atoms give off radiation by themselves.
institutions: École Nationale des Ponts et Chaussées

records.title: Eijkman traces beriberi to diet
records.note: Chickens fed polished rice fall ill and recover on unpolished rice, a path that led to the discovery of vitamins.

records.title: Buchner: fermentation without living cells
records.note: Juice pressed from yeast ferments sugar on its own: enzymes, not life itself, do the chemistry.

records.title: J. J. Thomson discovers the electron
records.note: Cathode rays are streams of particles far lighter than any atom, the first subatomic particle.

records.title: Ross: mosquitoes carry malaria
records.note: Malaria parasites in the gut of an Anopheles mosquito that had bitten an infected patient.

records.title: Marie and Pierre Curie discover polonium and radium
records.note: Tonnes of pitchblende processed by hand yield two new, intensely radioactive elements.

records.title: Aspirin
records.note: Acetylsalicylic acid, made at Bayer in 1897, goes on sale and becomes the world’s best-known drug.

records.title: Planck’s quantum hypothesis
records.note: Energy is given off in packets proportional to frequency, explaining the colour of hot bodies.

records.title: Landsteiner discovers blood groups
records.note: Red cells clump with some people’s serum but not others’: groups A, B and O make transfusion safe.

records.title: Annie Jump Cannon’s stellar classification
records.note: Stars sorted by their spectra into O, B, A, F, G, K, M; she classified some 350,000 by eye.

records.title: Bayliss and Starling discover hormones
records.note: Secretin, carried in the blood, sets the pancreas working: chemical messengers, named hormones in 1905.

records.title: Pavlov’s conditioned reflexes
records.note: Dogs learn to salivate at a signal that predicts food: learned reflexes can be measured.
records.place: S. M. Kirov Military Medical Academy
institutions: S. M. Kirov Military Medical Academy

records.title: Einthoven’s electrocardiograph
records.note: A string galvanometer records the heart’s electrical activity precisely.

records.title: The Wright brothers fly
records.note: The first sustained, controlled, powered flight of a heavier-than-air machine.

records.title: Tsiolkovsky’s rocket equation
records.note: The mathematics of reaching space with liquid-fuelled rockets in stages.

records.title: The vacuum tube
records.note: A two-electrode valve detects radio signals; with a third electrode, valves soon amplify them.

records.title: Einstein explains the photoelectric effect
records.note: Light comes in quanta, each able to knock out one electron, the work cited in his Nobel Prize.
records.place: Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property
institutions: Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property

records.title: Nettie Stevens finds the sex chromosomes
records.note: In mealworms the males carry a small Y chromosome: sex is set by chromosomes.

records.title: Einstein’s special relativity
records.note: Space and time depend on motion, light’s speed is the same for all observers, and mass is energy: E = mc².
records.place: Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property
institutions: Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property

records.title: Tsvet invents chromatography
records.note: Plant pigments separate into coloured bands as they wash through a column of chalk.

records.title: Oldham detects the Earth’s core
records.note: A shadow in earthquake waves on the far side of the Earth reveals a dense core at its centre.

records.title: Bakelite, the first fully synthetic plastic
records.note: Phenol and formaldehyde set into a hard, heat-proof material for the electrical age.

records.title: The Burgess Shale fossils
records.note: Exquisitely preserved soft-bodied animals from the Cambrian explosion of life.

records.title: Carlos Chagas describes Chagas disease
records.note: He identifies the parasite, the insect that carries it and the disease itself in a single study.

records.title: Haber makes ammonia from the air
records.note: Nitrogen and hydrogen combine under pressure over a catalyst; scaled up by Bosch, it now feeds billions.

records.title: Mohorovičić finds the base of the crust
records.note: Earthquake waves speed up suddenly tens of kilometres down: the boundary between crust and mantle.

records.title: Salvarsan, the first modern chemotherapy
records.note: Compound 606, found by systematic screening, cures syphilis: a “magic bullet”.

records.title: Morgan: genes lie on chromosomes
records.note: A white-eyed fruit fly passes its trait on with the X chromosome; the Fly Room goes on to map genes.

records.title: Rutherford discovers the atomic nucleus
records.note: Alpha particles bouncing back from gold foil show almost all of an atom’s mass sits in a tiny centre.

records.title: The Hertzsprung–Russell diagram
records.note: Plotting stars’ brightness against colour reveals the main sequence and the giants, the key to how stars evolve.

records.title: Superconductivity
records.note: Mercury cooled with liquid helium to 4 kelvin loses all electrical resistance.

records.title: Wegener proposes continental drift
records.note: Matching coastlines, fossils and rocks suggest the continents were once joined and have moved apart.

records.title: Hess discovers cosmic rays
records.note: Balloon flights to over 5 km show radiation increasing with height: it comes from space.

records.title: Slipher measures galaxies’ speeds
records.note: Spiral nebulae are rushing away at hundreds of kilometres a second, the first hint of cosmic expansion.

records.title: Leavitt’s period–luminosity law
records.note: Brighter Cepheid variable stars pulse more slowly, a yardstick for cosmic distances.

records.title: X-ray crystallography
records.note: Laue diffracts X-rays through crystals; the Braggs use it to read the positions of atoms.

records.title: Moseley’s atomic numbers
records.note: X-ray spectra order the elements by nuclear charge, fixing the periodic table and its gaps.

records.title: Bohr’s quantum atom
records.note: Electrons keep to fixed orbits and give off light when they jump between them, explaining hydrogen’s spectrum.

records.title: Ramanujan writes to Hardy
records.note: A Madras clerk’s letter full of extraordinary formulas begins one of mathematics’ great collaborations.

records.title: Alice Ball’s treatment for leprosy
records.note: An injectable form of chaulmoogra oil becomes the best leprosy treatment until the 1940s.

records.title: Einstein’s general relativity
records.note: Gravity is the curving of spacetime by mass and energy.

records.title: Schwarzschild’s black-hole solution
records.note: Weeks after Einstein’s theory, an exact solution around a point mass, with a radius from which nothing escapes.

records.title: Shapley moves the Sun from the Galaxy’s centre
records.note: Globular clusters centre on a point far off in Sagittarius: the Milky Way is huge and we are off to one side.

records.title: Noether’s theorem
records.note: Every symmetry of a physical system brings a conserved quantity, such as energy or momentum.

records.title: An eclipse confirms that gravity bends light
records.note: Stars near the eclipsed Sun appear shifted by the amount general relativity predicts.

records.title: Rutherford transmutes nitrogen
records.note: Alpha particles knock hydrogen nuclei out of nitrogen: the first artificial nuclear reaction, and the proton.

records.title: The Bergen school describes weather fronts
records.note: Storms form along the boundaries between masses of warm and cold air.

records.title: Milanković links ice ages to the Earth’s orbit
records.note: Slow cycles in the shape of the Earth’s orbit and the tilt of its axis pace the ice ages.

records.title: Saha’s ionisation equation
records.note: Temperature decides how ionised a star’s gases are, which explains the sequence of stellar spectra.

records.title: Insulin isolated
records.note: A pancreatic extract keeps diabetic dogs alive; within months it saves a dying boy.

records.title: Friedmann’s expanding universe
records.note: General relativity allows a universe that grows or shrinks rather than standing still.

records.title: The Compton effect
records.note: X-rays bouncing off electrons lose energy like colliding balls: light carries momentum.

records.title: Hubble shows there are other galaxies
records.note: Cepheid stars in the Andromeda nebula put it far outside the Milky Way: a universe of galaxies.

records.title: Bose–Einstein statistics
records.note: Counting light quanta as identical reproduces Planck’s law; particles that obey it are called bosons.

records.title: De Broglie’s matter waves
records.note: Electrons, and all matter, behave as waves with a wavelength set by their momentum.

records.title: The Taung Child
records.note: A child’s skull from South Africa with human-like teeth points to Africa as humanity’s birthplace.

records.title: Pauli’s exclusion principle
records.note: No two electrons can share the same quantum state, which gives the periodic table its structure.

records.title: Heisenberg’s matrix mechanics
records.note: The first complete form of quantum mechanics, built only from quantities that can be observed.

records.title: Cecilia Payne: stars are mostly hydrogen
records.note: Applying Saha’s equation to stellar spectra shows stars are made mainly of hydrogen and helium.

records.title: Goddard launches a liquid-fuelled rocket
records.note: A two-and-a-half-second flight from a farm opens the way to spaceflight.

records.title: Schrödinger’s wave equation
records.note: An equation for the wave function predicts the energy levels of atoms.

records.title: Lemaître: the universe is expanding
records.note: Galaxy redshifts and relativity imply expansion; in 1931 he traces it back to a “primeval atom”.

records.title: Heisenberg’s uncertainty principle
records.note: Position and momentum cannot both be known exactly: a limit set by nature, not by instruments.

records.title: Dirac’s equation predicts antimatter
records.note: Joining quantum mechanics with relativity explains the electron’s spin and predicts the positron.

records.title: Fleming discovers penicillin
records.note: A mould contaminating a culture plate kills the bacteria around it.

records.title: The Raman effect
records.note: Light scattered by molecules shifts in colour by amounts that identify the molecule.

records.title: Gerty and Carl Cori’s cycle
records.note: Lactate from working muscle is turned back into glucose by the liver.

records.title: Hubble: galaxies recede in proportion to distance
records.note: The farther a galaxy, the faster it moves away: the universe is expanding.

records.title: The Chandrasekhar limit
records.note: A white dwarf heavier than about 1.4 Suns cannot support itself and must collapse further.

records.title: Tombaugh discovers Pluto
records.note: Blinking between photographic plates reveals a faint moving point beyond Neptune.

records.title: Lawrence’s cyclotron
records.note: Particles spiral outwards in a magnetic field, gaining energy on every turn.

records.title: The electron microscope
records.note: Magnetic lenses focus beams of electrons, eventually showing detail far below the limit of light.

records.title: Gödel’s incompleteness theorems
records.note: Any consistent system strong enough for arithmetic contains true statements it cannot prove.

records.title: Chadwick discovers the neutron
records.note: A neutral particle in the nucleus explains atomic masses and becomes the key to fission.

records.title: Anderson finds the positron
records.note: A cloud-chamber track of a positive electron, the first antimatter, as Dirac predicted.

records.title: Jansky hears radio waves from the Milky Way
records.note: Static on a rotating antenna peaks towards the centre of the Galaxy: radio astronomy begins.

records.title: Cockcroft and Walton split the atom
records.note: Protons from an accelerator split lithium nuclei, and the energy released confirms E = mc².

records.title: Zwicky infers dark matter
records.note: Galaxies in the Coma Cluster move too fast to be held together by the matter we can see.

records.title: Kolmogorov’s axioms of probability
records.note: Probability rebuilt on measure theory, the foundation of modern statistics.
records.place: Schmidt Institute of Physics of the Earth
institutions: Schmidt Institute of Physics of the Earth
D. Mendeleev University of Chemical Technology of Russia

records.title: Irène and Frédéric Joliot-Curie make new radioactive atoms
records.note: Bombarding aluminium with alpha particles creates a radioactive form of phosphorus.

records.title: Yukawa’s theory of the nuclear force
records.note: A heavy particle passed between protons and neutrons explains the short reach of the strong force.

records.title: Nylon
records.note: A synthetic polymer fibre made at DuPont, the first to succeed commercially.

records.title: Domagk’s Prontosil, the first sulfa drug
records.note: A red dye cures streptococcal infections in mice and then people, the first widely effective antibacterial.

records.title: Watson-Watt’s radar
records.note: Radio echoes from a bomber flying near Daventry show aircraft can be detected far away.

records.title: The Richter magnitude scale
records.note: A logarithmic scale compares the sizes of earthquakes from seismograph readings.

records.title: Inge Lehmann discovers the inner core
records.note: Faint earthquake waves inside the core’s shadow reveal a solid inner core.

records.title: Turing’s universal machine
records.note: A simple imagined machine defines computation and shows some problems can never be solved by algorithm.

records.title: The jet engine
records.note: Whittle runs the first turbojet on a test bed; von Ohain’s engine powers the first jet flight in 1939.

records.title: The Krebs cycle
records.note: A loop of reactions in the cell burns fuel molecules to release energy.

records.title: Superfluidity
records.note: Liquid helium below 2.2 kelvin flows without any viscosity.
records.place: P.L. Kapitza Institute for Physical Problems RAS
institutions: P.L. Kapitza Institute for Physical Problems RAS

records.title: A living coelacanth
records.note: A fish known only from fossils 66 million years old turns up in a trawler’s catch off South Africa.

records.title: Nuclear fission
records.note: Uranium hit by neutrons yields barium; Meitner and Frisch explain it as the nucleus splitting in two.

records.title: Pauling’s Nature of the Chemical Bond
records.note: Quantum mechanics explains how atoms bond, with electronegativity and hybrid orbitals.

records.title: Marguerite Perey discovers francium
records.note: The last element to be discovered in nature, found in the decay of actinium.

records.title: Bethe explains how stars shine
records.note: Hydrogen fuses into helium through the proton–proton chain and the carbon cycle, powering the Sun.

records.title: Penicillin becomes a medicine
records.note: Purified penicillin protects infected mice; mass production follows in time for D-Day.
records.place: Sir William Dunn School of Pathology
institutions: Sir William Dunn School of Pathology

records.title: Plutonium and the first elements beyond uranium
records.note: Neptunium and plutonium, heavier than uranium, are made with the cyclotron.

records.title: Zuse’s Z3, a programmable computer
records.note: An electromechanical machine that runs programs from punched film, in binary floating point.

records.title: The first nuclear chain reaction
records.note: A pile of graphite and uranium under a Chicago stadium sustains a controlled chain reaction.

records.title: Frequency-hopping radio
records.note: A patent for jam-proof radio guidance that hops between frequencies, a forerunner of modern wireless.

records.title: Colossus, an electronic code-breaking computer
records.note: Valve machines help break the German high command’s cipher.

records.title: Kolff’s artificial kidney
records.note: A rotating-drum dialyser, built under occupation, keeps patients with failing kidneys alive.

records.title: Streptomycin, the first drug against tuberculosis
records.note: Isolated from soil bacteria by the student Albert Schatz in Waksman’s laboratory.

records.title: DNA carries genetic information
records.note: Purified DNA turns harmless bacteria into virulent ones: genes are made of DNA.

records.title: The first nuclear explosion
records.note: The Manhattan Project’s test in New Mexico releases energy equal to about twenty thousand tonnes of TNT.

records.title: ENIAC
records.note: A general-purpose electronic computer of some 18,000 valves, programmed by a team of six women.

records.title: The Monte Carlo method
records.note: Random sampling on early computers solves problems too complex for exact methods.

records.title: The transistor
records.note: A germanium device amplifies signals, replacing valves and making modern electronics possible.

records.title: Big Bang nucleosynthesis
records.note: A hot early universe would forge hydrogen and helium in the observed amounts and leave a faint afterglow.

records.title: Shannon’s information theory
records.note: Information measured in bits, and the limits to sending it reliably over a noisy channel.

records.title: The first stored-program computer
records.note: The Manchester Baby runs a program held in its own electronic memory.

records.title: Quantum electrodynamics
records.note: Renormalisation tames the infinities, making QED the most precisely tested theory in physics.

records.title: Radiocarbon dating
records.note: The steady decay of carbon-14 dates once-living material up to about 50,000 years old.

records.title: The nuclear shell model
records.note: Protons and neutrons fill shells, explaining the “magic numbers” of especially stable nuclei.

records.title: McClintock’s jumping genes
records.note: In maize, some pieces of DNA move around the genome and switch other genes on and off.
institutions: Cornell University College of Agriculture and Life Sciences

records.title: The first computer weather forecast
records.note: ENIAC computes a 24-hour forecast, the start of numerical weather prediction.

records.title: HeLa, the first immortal human cell line
records.note: Cells taken without consent from Henrietta Lacks’s tumour grow indefinitely and power decades of research.

records.title: Radio waves from cold hydrogen
records.note: The 21-centimetre line lets radio astronomers map the spiral arms of the Milky Way.

records.title: Grace Hopper’s first compiler
records.note: A program that translates symbolic code into machine instructions, leading to languages such as COBOL.

records.title: The Hershey–Chase experiment
records.note: Radioactive labels show that viruses inject their DNA, not their protein, into bacteria.

records.title: The Miller–Urey experiment
records.note: Sparks through simple gases produce amino acids: the building blocks of life from chemistry alone.

records.title: Nerve growth factor
records.note: A substance from mouse tumours makes nerve fibres sprout, the first growth factor known.

records.title: Rosalind Franklin’s Photo 51
records.note: An X-ray diffraction image of DNA whose cross-shaped pattern reveals a helix.

records.title: The DNA double helix
records.note: Two complementary strands wound in a helix suggest at once how genetic information is copied.

records.title: Marie Tharp finds the Mid-Atlantic rift
records.note: Plotting sonar soundings reveals a valley along the crest of the ridge, evidence that the seafloor spreads.

records.title: The silicon solar cell
records.note: Sunlight turned into electricity at about 6% efficiency, the first practical solar cell.

records.title: The caesium atomic clock
records.note: Time kept by the vibrations of caesium atoms; in 1967 the second itself is redefined by them.

records.title: Sanger sequences insulin
records.note: The first full amino-acid sequence of a protein: every protein has a precise chemical structure.

records.title: Salk’s polio vaccine
records.note: A trial involving well over a million children shows the inactivated vaccine works.

records.title: The age of the Earth
records.note: Lead isotopes in meteorites give 4.55 billion years; Patterson goes on to expose lead pollution.

records.title: The neutrino detected
records.note: Antineutrinos from a nuclear reactor are caught in tanks of water, 26 years after Pauli proposed them.

records.title: Dorothy Hodgkin solves vitamin B12
records.note: X-ray crystallography and early computers reveal the structure of a large, vital molecule.

records.title: How stars make the elements
records.note: Nuclear reactions in stars and supernovae build every element heavier than helium.

records.title: The BCS theory of superconductivity
records.note: Electrons pair up through vibrations of the crystal and move without resistance.

records.title: Wu shows nature tells left from right
records.note: Electrons from decaying cobalt-60 prefer one direction, overturning the conservation of parity.

records.title: Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite
records.note: A small beeping sphere in orbit opens the space age.
institutions: S.P. Korolev Rocket and Space Corporation Energia

records.title: The integrated circuit
records.note: Kilby’s germanium chip, then Noyce’s planar silicon one, put whole circuits on a single piece of semiconductor.

records.title: The Keeling curve
records.note: Continuous measurements show the carbon dioxide in the air rising year after year.

records.title: The Van Allen radiation belts
records.note: Explorer 1’s Geiger counter finds zones of trapped charged particles around the Earth.

records.title: Mary Leakey finds “Nutcracker Man”
records.note: A robust 1.8-million-year-old skull at Olduvai Gorge pushes human origins deep into Africa’s past.

records.title: Radioimmunoassay
records.note: Radioactive tracers measure tiny amounts of hormones in blood, transforming endocrinology.

records.title: Jane Goodall sees chimpanzees make tools
records.note: A chimpanzee strips a twig to fish for termites: making tools is not uniquely human.

records.title: The laser
records.note: A ruby crystal produces the first coherent beam of light.

records.title: Cracking the genetic code
records.note: Synthetic RNA made only of uracil yields a chain of phenylalanine; by 1966 all 64 codons are read.
records.place: United States National Institutes of Health
institutions: United States National Institutes of Health

records.title: How genes are switched on and off
records.note: A regulatory switch in bacteria shows how cells control which genes are active.

records.title: Gagarin, the first human in space
records.note: One orbit of the Earth in 108 minutes.
institutions: S.P. Korolev Rocket and Space Corporation Energia

records.title: Green fluorescent protein
records.note: A glowing jellyfish protein, isolated by Shimomura, later becomes a universal tag for watching genes at work.

records.title: Rachel Carson’s Silent Spring
records.note: The harm pesticides such as DDT do to wildlife launches the modern environmental movement.

records.title: Lorenz discovers chaos
records.note: A simple weather model is so sensitive to its starting point that long-range forecasting is impossible.

records.title: Quasars
records.note: The spectrum of 3C 273 is hugely redshifted: a starlike point billions of light-years away, outshining galaxies.

records.title: Magnetic stripes confirm seafloor spreading
records.note: Stripes on the ocean floor record new crust forming at ridges while the Earth’s magnetic field flips.

records.title: The cosmic microwave background
records.note: A faint microwave hiss from every direction is the afterglow of the Big Bang.

records.title: The Higgs mechanism
records.note: A field filling space gives particles their mass and implies a new particle.

records.title: The quark model
records.note: Protons, neutrons and their relatives are built from three kinds of smaller particle.

records.title: The fast Fourier transform
records.note: An algorithm that makes digital signal processing fast enough to be everywhere.

records.title: Kevlar
records.note: A liquid-crystal polymer solution spun into fibres five times stronger than steel for their weight.

records.title: Optical fibre communication
records.note: Kao shows that purified glass fibres could carry light signals over long distances.

records.title: Manabe’s climate model
records.note: The first realistic computer model of the atmosphere predicts about 2 °C of warming if carbon dioxide doubles.

records.title: Electroweak unification
records.note: Electromagnetism and the weak force are two faces of one interaction, a pillar of the Standard Model.

records.title: Lynn Margulis: cells merged to build complex life
records.note: Mitochondria and chloroplasts began as free-living bacteria taken inside other cells.

records.title: The first human heart transplant
records.note: In Cape Town, Louis Washkansky receives a donor heart and lives for 18 days.

records.title: Plate tectonics
records.note: The Earth’s surface is a mosaic of rigid plates whose motions explain earthquakes, volcanoes and mountains.

records.title: Jocelyn Bell Burnell discovers pulsars
records.note: A radio source ticking every 1.34 seconds turns out to be a spinning neutron star.

records.title: Kimura’s neutral theory of molecular evolution
records.note: Most changes in DNA are neither helpful nor harmful and spread by chance.

records.title: Oral rehydration therapy
records.note: A drink of water, salt and sugar saves cholera patients; it goes on to save millions of children.
institutions: Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health

records.title: Apollo 11 lands on the Moon
records.note: Humans walk on another world; the guidance software led by Margaret Hamilton copes with alarms during the landing.

records.title: ARPANET carries its first message
records.note: A computer at UCLA sends “lo” to Stanford before crashing: the internet’s ancestor.

records.title: The charge-coupled device
records.note: An image sensor that turned photography and astronomy digital.

records.title: Reverse transcriptase
records.note: Some viruses copy RNA back into DNA, breaking the one-way flow of genetic information.

records.title: Vera Rubin’s galaxy rotation curves
records.note: Stars at the edge of Andromeda orbit as fast as those near the centre: evidence for dark matter.

records.title: The CT scanner
records.note: X-ray slices put together by computer give the first cross-sectional image of a living brain.

records.title: The first strong black-hole candidate
records.note: A star orbiting an unseen companion too heavy to be a neutron star.

records.title: The microprocessor
records.note: A whole computer processor on one chip of 2,300 transistors.

records.title: NP-completeness
records.note: Some problems are as hard as every problem whose answers are easy to check: the P versus NP question.

records.title: Tu Youyou discovers artemisinin
records.note: A fourth-century herbal text leads her to a cold extract of sweet wormwood that cures malaria.

records.title: Yuan Longping’s hybrid rice
records.note: Hybrid rice raises yields by about a fifth, helping to feed hundreds of millions.

records.title: Magnetic resonance imaging
records.note: Magnetic field gradients turn nuclear magnetic resonance into images of the body.

records.title: Recombinant DNA
records.note: Genes cut and pasted into bacterial plasmids are copied by the bacteria: genetic engineering begins.

records.title: Asymptotic freedom completes the Standard Model
records.note: Quarks bind ever more weakly at short range, making the theory of the strong force work.

records.title: CFCs threaten the ozone layer
records.note: Chlorine from refrigerant gases destroys ozone high in the atmosphere in a chain reaction.

records.title: Hawking radiation
records.note: Quantum effects make black holes glow faintly and slowly evaporate.

records.title: Lucy, Australopithecus afarensis
