records.note: A 3.2-million-year-old skeleton shows our ancestors walked upright long before their brains grew large.

records.title: TCP/IP joins networks into an internet
records.note: A protocol for linking separate networks into one, adopted across ARPANET in 1983.

records.title: Mandelbrot’s fractals
records.note: Self-similar shapes describe coastlines, clouds and markets; he coins the word “fractal”.

records.title: Monoclonal antibodies
records.note: Immune cells fused with cancer cells make unlimited amounts of a single antibody.

records.title: The four colour theorem proved by computer
records.note: The first major theorem proved with essential help from a computer.

records.title: Public-key cryptography
records.note: Two parties agree a secret over an open line; RSA follows a year later.

records.title: Endo discovers the first statin
records.note: A compound from a mould blocks the body’s cholesterol production; statins become among the most used drugs.
records.place: Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology
institutions: Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology

records.title: Woese discovers the archaea
records.note: Ribosomal RNA reveals a third domain of life alongside bacteria and eukaryotes.

records.title: Life at hydrothermal vents
records.note: The submersible Alvin finds rich communities living on chemical energy from the vents, not sunlight.

records.title: Sanger DNA sequencing
records.note: Chain-terminating nucleotides read DNA letter by letter; the first DNA genome follows.

records.title: The Voyager probes
records.note: Twin spacecraft tour Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune; Voyager 1 reaches interstellar space in 2012.

records.title: The first baby conceived by IVF
records.note: Louise Brown is born after fertilisation outside the body.

records.title: Avermectin, later ivermectin
records.note: A soil microbe from Japan yields a drug against river blindness and elephantiasis.
institutions: Faculty of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Tokyo University of Science

records.title: An asteroid ended the age of dinosaurs
records.note: A layer of clay rich in iridium, first studied at Gubbio, marks a giant impact 66 million years ago.

records.title: Genes that lay out the embryo
records.note: A search through fruit-fly mutants finds the genes that set up the body plan.

records.title: Cosmic inflation
records.note: A burst of runaway expansion in the first instant explains why the universe is so uniform and flat.

records.title: The quantum Hall effect
records.note: Electrical resistance comes in exact steps set only by fundamental constants.

records.title: Smallpox eradicated
records.note: The first human disease wiped out, after a worldwide campaign of vaccination and surveillance.

records.title: The scanning tunnelling microscope
records.note: A tip a few atoms wide images individual atoms on a surface.

records.title: Aspect’s test of Bell’s inequalities
records.note: Entangled photons break Bell’s limit: quantum correlations cannot be explained by hidden local causes.

records.title: Bacteria cause stomach ulcers
records.note: Helicobacter pylori, not stress, causes most ulcers; Marshall drinks a culture to prove it.

records.title: Prions
records.note: Misfolded proteins, with no genetic material, cause infectious brain diseases.

records.title: Quasicrystals
records.note: An alloy with five-fold symmetry, ordered but never repeating, a pattern thought impossible.
records.place: National Institute of Standards and Technology

records.title: HIV identified
records.note: A new retrovirus isolated from a patient’s lymph node turns out to cause AIDS.

records.title: The polymerase chain reaction
records.note: Cycles of heating and copying multiply a stretch of DNA a billion times over.

records.title: W and Z bosons discovered
records.note: The carriers of the weak force are found at the masses the theory predicted.

records.title: DNA fingerprinting
records.note: Repeated stretches of DNA give a pattern unique to each person.

records.title: Telomerase
records.note: An enzyme that rebuilds the ends of chromosomes, linking cell ageing and cancer.

records.title: Chirped pulse amplification
records.note: Stretching, amplifying and squeezing laser pulses gives ultra-short, ultra-intense light, now used in eye surgery.

records.title: Buckminsterfullerene
records.note: Sixty carbon atoms form a hollow ball: a new form of carbon.

records.title: The lithium-ion battery
records.note: Building on Whittingham’s and Goodenough’s electrodes, Yoshino makes a safe, rechargeable cell.

records.title: The Antarctic ozone hole
records.note: Spring ozone over Antarctica has fallen by a third; the Montreal Protocol follows in 1987.

records.title: High-temperature superconductors
records.note: A copper-oxide ceramic superconducts at 35 kelvin, far above any metal; others soon pass liquid-nitrogen temperature.

records.title: Supernova 1987A
records.note: The nearest supernova in centuries; neutrinos from the collapsing core are detected on Earth.

records.title: The Vostok ice core
records.note: Bubbles of ancient air show carbon dioxide and temperature rising and falling together for 160,000 years.

records.title: The World Wide Web
records.note: A proposal for linked hypertext over the internet, with the first browser and server running by 1990.

records.title: The Hubble Space Telescope
records.note: Above the atmosphere, once its mirror is corrected, it measures the age and expansion of the universe.

records.title: The Chicxulub crater identified
records.note: A buried crater some 180 km wide in Yucatán is the impact behind the extinction of the dinosaurs.

records.title: Ripples in the cosmic microwave background
records.note: COBE measures the background’s perfect heat spectrum and the tiny ripples that seeded galaxies.

records.title: The Kuiper belt
records.note: The first object found beyond Neptune after Pluto reveals a belt of icy bodies.

records.title: The first planets beyond the Solar System
records.note: Timing a pulsar reveals planets of a few Earth masses orbiting it.

records.title: The bright blue LED
records.note: Gallium nitride LEDs complete the set of colours, making white LED lighting possible.

records.title: Wiles proves Fermat’s Last Theorem
records.note: A 350-year-old problem falls through the modularity of elliptic curves.

records.title: Shor’s quantum factoring algorithm
records.note: A quantum computer could factor large numbers exponentially faster, threatening today’s encryption.

records.title: A planet around a Sun-like star
records.note: A giant planet on a four-day orbit, found by the wobble it gives its star.

records.title: A Bose–Einstein condensate is made
records.note: Rubidium atoms cooled to billionths of a degree merge into a single quantum state.

records.title: Dolly the sheep
records.note: The first mammal cloned from an adult cell.

records.title: Feathered dinosaurs
records.note: Sinosauropteryx from north-east China shows simple feathers on a dinosaur, tying dinosaurs to birds.

records.title: The universe’s expansion is speeding up
records.note: Distant supernovae are fainter than expected, pointing to a mysterious dark energy.

records.title: Human embryonic stem cells
records.note: Cells able to become any tissue are grown in the laboratory.

records.title: Neutrinos have mass
records.note: Neutrinos change type as they travel, which requires them to have mass.

records.title: RNA interference
records.note: Double-stranded RNA silences matching genes, a new layer of gene control.

records.title: The structure of the ribosome
records.note: Atomic maps of the cell’s protein factory, after decades of work.
institutions: University of Utah School of Medicine

records.title: The Hubble constant pinned down
records.note: The Hubble Space Telescope Key Project measures the universe’s expansion rate to about ten per cent.

records.title: A giant black hole at the Milky Way’s centre
records.note: Stars orbiting an unseen object of four million solar masses show it must be a black hole.

records.title: The Human Genome Project completed
records.note: An international consortium reads the three billion letters of human DNA.
records.place: United States National Institutes of Health
institutions: United States National Institutes of Health

records.title: Perelman proves the Poincaré conjecture
records.note: Ricci flow settles a century-old question about three-dimensional shapes; he declines the Fields Medal.
institutions: St. Petersburg Department of Steklov Institute of Mathematics of Russian Academy of Sciences

records.title: Graphene isolated
records.note: Sticky tape peels carbon into sheets one atom thick, astonishingly strong and conductive.

records.title: Tiktaalik, a fish on its way to land
records.note: A 375-million-year-old fish with a neck and limb-like fins, found where theory said to look.

records.title: Grid cells, the brain’s coordinate system
records.note: Neurons fire on a hexagonal grid as an animal moves, letting the brain map space.
records.place: Norwegian University of Science and Technology
institutions: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

records.title: Induced pluripotent stem cells
records.note: Four genes turn adult skin cells back into stem cells.

records.title: Water found across the Moon’s surface
records.note: Instruments on India’s Chandrayaan-1 detect water and hydroxyl across the lunar surface.

records.title: The Neanderthal genome
records.note: Ancient DNA shows people outside Africa carry some Neanderthal genes; the Denisovans are identified the same year.
records.place: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology
institutions: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology

records.title: CRISPR–Cas9 genome editing
records.note: A bacterial enzyme guided by RNA cuts DNA at any chosen spot.

records.title: Deep learning wins at image recognition
records.note: A deep neural network trained on graphics chips wins the ImageNet challenge by a wide margin.

records.title: The Higgs boson discovered
records.note: The ATLAS and CMS experiments at the Large Hadron Collider find the particle predicted in 1964.

records.title: Bounded gaps between primes
records.note: Infinitely many pairs of primes lie less than 70 million apart, a first step towards the twin prime conjecture.

records.title: Mirzakhani’s geometry of curved surfaces
records.note: Work on the dynamics and geometry of Riemann surfaces makes her the first woman to win the Fields Medal.

records.title: Gravitational waves detected
records.note: Ripples in spacetime from two merging black holes, a century after Einstein predicted them.

records.title: Homo naledi
records.note: Fossils of a new human species from a deep chamber of a South African cave.

records.title: An orbital rocket booster lands upright
records.note: A first stage returns to land after a launch to orbit, making rockets reusable.

records.title: Viazovska solves sphere packing in eight dimensions
records.note: Using modular forms she proves the E8 lattice is the densest packing in eight dimensions.

records.title: The Transformer neural network
records.note: A design built on attention that underlies today’s large language models.

records.title: The first image of a black hole
records.note: A planet-wide array of radio dishes images the shadow of the black hole in the galaxy M87.

records.title: AlphaFold predicts protein structures
records.note: An AI system predicts the 3D shapes of proteins from their sequences with near-experimental accuracy.

records.title: mRNA vaccines
records.note: Modified messenger RNA, made safe by Karikó and Weissman, gives COVID-19 vaccines within a year.

records.title: DART nudges an asteroid
records.note: A deliberate collision shortens the orbit of Dimorphos, the first test of planetary defence.

records.title: Fusion ignition
records.note: Laser-driven fusion releases more energy than the lasers deliver to the fuel.

records.title: The James Webb Space Telescope’s first images
records.note: An infrared observatory 1.5 million km away sees galaxies from the universe’s first few hundred million years.

records.title: A landing near the Moon’s south pole
records.note: India’s Chandrayaan-3 makes the first soft landing in the Moon’s south polar region.

records.title: Samples from the far side of the Moon
records.note: China’s Chang’e 6 brings back the first rock and soil from the lunar far side.

records.title: The complete wiring of a fly’s brain
records.note: The FlyWire project maps all 140,000 neurons and some 50 million connections of an adult fruit fly.

records.title: The geometric Langlands conjecture proved
records.note: A team of nine mathematicians completes a proof of some 800 pages connecting geometry and number theory.

records.title: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory’s first light
records.note: The largest digital camera ever built begins a ten-year survey of the southern sky.
